text:
Alex Tuch leads Washington with 14 goals in 21 games in his first season as a Capital, including a short-handed goal against Jeremy Swayman in Boston on Nov. 21 and two points against his former club, Buffalo, two nights earlier. He has goals in three straight games.

The goals carry a footnote: 14 on 10.4 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 25% against 17% last season, and our talent range puts his true rate near 16%. The chances themselves are real, up to 1.56 expected goals per 60 from 0.91 a year ago, and Washington takes 55.7% of the expected goals at five on five with him on.

The odd part is the assists: three all season. Washington has scored 5.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which usually swings back, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man last season (87th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists). With the Capitals on a five-game losing streak, watch for the passing to start showing up.
